subject: Residency + KMS: blind-sign capability inquiry & PrivateLink evidence
messages:
From: Julie Kim <julie.kim@kestrelhealth.com>
To: avery_johnson@redwood.example
Date: 2026-08-26T09:12:00Z
Subject: Residency + KMS question for our security pack

Hi Avery —

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier. We are assembling the SIG/CAIQ packet for Kestrel's internal legal/security review and have two items we need clarified before we can proceed: 

1) Key management details: we saw on the call that Redwood supports HSM-backed signing. Our security team specifically asked whether Redwood supports a "blinded-signing" flow (i.e., a signing operation where the key holder cannot see plaintext) for certain regulatory workloads, or alternately whether you can provide deterministic remote signing with an audit attestation. If true, can you point to the runbook or describe the exact controls (exportability, BYOK options, rotation windows, access approvals)?

2) Private connectivity evidence: we need a short diagram or checklist showing how PrivateLink/VPC peering is configured for EU-hosted tenants, including operator access controls and egress restrictions. 

If you can send a short artefact (1–2 pages) describing the above and any SOC2/SIG artifact references, we can move to procurement. Markus (cc) will handle contractual items.

Best,
Julie
Security & Privacy Lead
Kestrel Health
From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.example>
To: Julie Kim <julie.kim@kestrelhealth.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.example, rachel_kim@redwood.example
Date: 2026-08-26T15:04:00Z
Subject: Re: Residency + KMS question for our security pack

Julie —

Thanks for the clear ask. I'm looping in Neha (infosec) and Rachel (cloud ops) for the technical artifacts. High-level answers up front:

- We do not perform plaintext key export from our HSMs for tenant master keys; keys are non-exportable when provisioned in our HSM cluster.
- We support quarterly rotation by default, accelerated rotations on request, and BYOK via customer-imported KEKs under an HSM-wrapped envelope (operator approval required).
- We do not call our signing mode "blind signing" in product docs; however, we do offer an HSM-backed remote signing API with attestation logs and a short-lived signing token model that prevents operators from viewing payload content. Neha will add detail on attestation and auditability.

Rachel will attach a PrivateLink diagram and the ops checklist for EU tenancy. Expect a short package from us by EOD tomorrow.

Cheers,
Avery
Director, Solutions
Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.example>
To: Julie Kim <julie.kim@kestrelhealth.com>, Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.example>
Cc: rachel_kim@redwood.example, irene_choi@redwood.example
Date: 2026-08-27T10:22:00Z
Subject: KMS attestation notes + rotation runbook (draft)

Julie —

Following up with the KMS specifics you asked for. I've attached a short runbook (kms-rotation-runbook.md) and a one-page summary (residency_evidence_summary.pdf). Key points: 

- HSM model & export: keys for tenant Master Key Encryption Keys (KEKs) are created in an AWS CloudHSM/partner HSM pool with non-exportable flags. We do offer a BYOK import where a customer wraps a key with a hardware-wrapped envelope during provisioning; we never unwrap keys in plaintext in our control plane.
- Signing API (attestation): our signing operation uses an ephemeral, purpose-bound signing session. Operators cannot retrieve plaintext content via the service: the signing token is validated by the HSM and the operation produces an HSM attestation statement (timestamped). This provides the audit trail equivalent of a blinded-signing workflow for regulatory reviewers.

- Rotation: default quarterly rotation for tenant KEKs, optional monthly for high-risk customers. Rotation is staged: pre-rotation snapshot -> rewrap -> smoke tests -> promote -> post-rotation audit. The runbook contains action owners and a 24-hour rollback window.

- Access controls: keystore admin operations are gated behind ticketed workflows, 2-person approval for any manual key action, and logs are forwarded to an immutable SIEM endpoint (retention 2 years by default for EU contracts).

I'll also attach the SOC2 evidence index (redacted) to the Drive folder and a short note about how attestations are surfaced in our compliance portal.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Security Engineer
Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-08-28T08:46:00Z
Subject: PrivateLink diagram and operator boundary checklist

Julie —

Attached is a PrivateLink architecture diagram (privatelink-architecture-diagram.png) and a short operator boundary checklist in the Drive link. Highlights: 

- EU tenancy runs in a dedicated VPC per-customer with PrivateLink endpoints in the customer's account or VPC-peering as requested. We support both single-tenant VPCs (for Dedicated) and logically isolated stacks for Hosted with strict routing controls.
- Operator access: no operator-level SSH into tenant VMs; access for maintenance goes through a bastion service with time-limited ephemeral credentials and just-in-time access. Router/egress ACLs block outbound flows to non-whitelisted IP ranges; egress to third-party integrations must be explicitly enabled in the tenancy contract.
- Evidence: we've uploaded the SOC 2 artifact index (redacted) and the SIG self-assessment link to the drive.

Let us know if you'd like an on-call window demo of the JIT access flow.

Rachel Kim
Cloud Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
